title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sits in a dossier on the functional equation of L-functions in the geometric case. The facing pages are a Bourbaki Commutative Algebra draft (Ch. VII, divisors and pseudo-null modules) used as scrap paper and are unrelated.

1) Global functional equation. Grothendieck writes L_{E_y}(1/(qt)) = A(t) L_{E_y}(t). Here E_y is an object (an l-adic sheaf, a motive, or the fibre of a family at y) over a base over F_q. A(t) is the global 'epsilon factor', in its geometric form: a monomial c·t^n with n an Euler characteristic.

2) Factoring A(t) over special points x. A finite set of points x carries local data alpha_x(E_y). Each has its own local L-function L_{alpha_x(E_y)}(t), Euler-characteristic-type invariant chi_x(E_y) and constant delta_x(E_y). He writes
 A(t) = prod_x [L_{alpha_x}(t^{-1}) / L_{alpha_x}(p^{-s}t)] · (-t)^{chi^phi(E_y) - sum_x chi_x(E_y)} · q^{chi^phi(E_y)} / (delta^phi(E_y) · prod_x delta_x(E_y)^{-1}).
- chi^phi is a global Euler characteristic, corrected by the local contributions chi_x.
- delta^phi is a global constant.
- p^s is apparently the local Frobenius norm (residue field size) at x.

3) Local functional equation. Each local factor obeys L_{alpha_x}(1/(p^s t)) = A_x(t) L_{alpha_x}(t). The circled ratio is identified with A_x(t^{-1})^{-1}. This checks: substitute t -> t^{-1} in the local equation to get L(p^{-s}t) = A_x(t^{-1}) L(t^{-1}). So the global constant is a product of a 'corrected global' monomial and inverse local epsilon-type factors.

4) N.B. (hard to read). Treating the local factor lambda_x(E_y)(t) as a 'piece' loses the additivity condition, so it is better not to form it directly. This is about keeping invariants additive in exact sequences, as Euler characteristics and determinants are.

5) Program ('Pb').
- (a) In the classical geometric cases, construct the alpha_x(E_y) that determine the local factors lambda_x(E_y)(t). Compute chi_x, delta_x and the absolute values (weights) of the Frobenius eigenvalues.
- (b) Give a general Grothendieck–Ogg(-Shafarevich)-type formula for chi^phi(E_y), the 'global dimension'.
- (c) Give a formula for delta^phi(E_y), the 'arithmetic constant'.

In modern terms this is the program of determining the constant of the functional equation of geometric L-functions via local data:
- Euler–Poincaré / conductor formulas: Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich; Deligne–Milnor for isolated singularities.
- A product formula for the constant in terms of local constants: Langlands–Deligne local constants; Laumon's 1987 product formula; later work by T. Saito and others on epsilon factors and discriminants.
- Weights of local Frobenius eigenvalues: Weil II, local monodromy.
errors: No mathematical error detected in what is written. The identification of the circled ratio with A_x(t^{-1})^{-1} is consistent with the local functional equation as stated.
The exact meaning of p^{-s} (local norm vs. a twist) and of E_y and alpha_x is not fixed on the page, so the global formula is schematic rather than a precise statement.
The formula is posited, not proved; the 'Pb' list shows the local objects are not yet constructed.

ideas.what: Expressing the constant of the global functional equation of a geometric L-function as a product of local constants and local L-factor ratios at special points, times a q-power governed by an Euler characteristic
ideas.modern_name: Product formula for epsilon factors (global epsilon = q^{...} prod local epsilon)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands (local constants, unpublished, 1970); Deligne (1972-73, 'Les constantes des équations fonctionnelles des fonctions L'); Laumon (1987, geometric product formula)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's Bourbaki talk 279 (1964) and SGA 5 give rationality and the functional equation with an undetermined global constant; an explicit local factorisation is not there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Local functional equation L_{alpha_x}(1/(p^s t)) = A_x(t) L_{alpha_x}(t) for local objects attached to points x
ideas.modern_name: Local epsilon factors / local functional equations (local Tate duality / Tate thesis analogue)

ideas.what: Request for a general Grothendieck–Ogg formula for the global Euler characteristic chi^phi(E_y) with local corrections chi_x
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula; Deligne–Milnor formula; Kato–Saito conductor formula
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Ogg, Shafarevich (1963-65; SGA 5 exp. X); Deligne (SGA 7, Milnor formula); Kato–Saito (2000s)

ideas.what: Request for a formula for the global 'arithmetic constant' delta^phi(E_y)
ideas.modern_name: Determinant of cohomology / epsilon constant; discriminant formulas
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Laumon; T. Saito (discriminant of hypersurfaces, epsilon factors)

ideas.what: Determine absolute values (weights) of local Frobenius eigenvalues on local factors

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, as an explicit problem list, the factorisation of the constant of the global functional equation of a geometric L-function into local constants at special points. He also asks for local Euler-characteristic invariants, local constants and local weights. This amounts to a geometric product-formula program, written down independently of (and possibly before) Langlands–Deligne local constants and Laumon's product formula.
missed.quote: c) Donner une formule pour δ^φ(E_y) ... constante arithm.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's own route to the local–global structure of epsilon factors. The schematic 'corrected' exponent chi^phi - sum chi_x and constant delta^phi·prod delta_x^{-1} for families E_y may correspond to settings such as fibres with isolated singularities, where explicit formulas (T. Saito's work on discriminants and epsilon factors) are still being developed.

missed.claim: The N.B. warns that treating the local factor lambda_x(E_y)(t) as a 'piece' destroys additivity. This hints at a preference for defining local invariants additively, as in a K-theoretic / determinant-line formulation (later Deligne's determinant of cohomology).
missed.quote: on en perd la condition additive
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Consistent with, but not clearly anticipating, Deligne's determinant-functor formulation of local constants; low confidence given the illegible text.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear, early-looking problem statement for the local factorisation of the global constant (product formula) and local Euler characteristics, in Grothendieck's hand. The general idea is now standard and credited to Langlands/Deligne/Laumon. The date range (1962–1971+) is uncertain and the objects are not defined, so priority claims are weak.
transcription_corrections: The circled ratio's identification '= A_x(t^{-1})^{-1}' is correctly read and is mathematically consistent with the local equation below it.
'p^{-s}' / 'p^s' may be 'p^{-f}' or a local norm symbol; the letter in the exponent is unclear in the image.
Constant factor: numerator q^{chi^phi(E_y)}, denominator delta^phi(E_y)·prod_x delta_x(E_y)^{-1}; the '[?]' after the q-power is unnecessary.
N.B. line plausibly reads: 'Ayant écrit λ_x(E_y)(t) comme un morceau, on en perd la condition additive. Il vaut sans doute mieux ne pas former ... directement ...' (very uncertain).

Pb a): 'Dans les cas géométriques classiques, construire les α_x(E_y) qui déterminent les fns. dans les λ_x(E_y)(t). Déterminer en particulier χ_x(E_y), δ_x(E_y), les valeurs absolues des val. propres de Frobenius.' The marginal labels 'dimension globale' and 'constante arithm.' are linked by arrows from χ^φ(E_y) in b) and δ^φ(E_y) in c).
b) reads approximately 'Donner une formule générale Grothendieck–Ogg pour χ^φ(E_y)'.
